articles.title: Asset handover SOP
body: Use this procedure whenever custody of a tagged asset changes. Complete the digital handover form, capture both signatures, and generate the PDF receipt before updating inventory status.
Required fields: asset tag, from/to identity, reason (Onboarding, Transfer, Offboarding, Loan), condition notes, accessories checklist, and dual acknowledgement.
Validation: recipient cannot match donor; condition notes required when status is Damaged; at least one accessory or “None” must be selected.
After submit, the system writes a timeline event, links the PDF under Documents, and notifies both parties. Sample AI can draft condition notes — always review before signing.

articles.title: Laptop power & battery triage
body: Confirm the wall outlet is live and the adapter’s LED is solid green. A blinking LED usually points to a firmware handshake failure — try a known-good outlet and a different surge strip before swapping adapters.

Battery health below 80% of design capacity triggers the “Consider replacement” banner in the inventory detail. For MacBook fleets run `battery -l` from the dock; for ThinkPad fleets use Lenovo Vantage.

If the laptop will not power on with a verified adapter, perform an SMC reset (Intel) or a shutdown with the Touch ID button held 10 seconds (Apple Silicon). Persistent failure routes to depot repair.

articles.title: VPN stability on remote endpoints
body: Always run the latest GA client — 5.2.x or newer. Clients older than 12 months are not permitted to connect to the corporate gateway.
Enable split-tunnel only for the services that need it (Zoom, Teams, public docs). The default profile routes all corporate traffic through the tunnel; only override per the matrix in the KB.
If a session drops repeatedly, capture a packet trace with the bundled `vpn-diag` script and attach it to the ticket. The script redacts PII before writing the trace.

articles.title: Badge reader offline recovery
body: When a lobby reader goes offline, the controller’s heartbeat LED blinks red twice per second. The first line of recovery is a soft reset: hold the recessed button for 5 seconds until the LED turns solid green.
If the reader is still offline after the soft reset, check the PoE budget on the switch — readers on shared drops frequently lose power when a neighbouring device ramps up.
A hard reset (power cycle from the panel) should be the last resort. After a hard reset, the controller takes 3–4 minutes to re-register; budget that time before opening a ticket.

articles.title: External monitor flicker on MacBook
body: Most flicker reports are caused by an EDID handshake failure between the dock and the panel. Update the dock firmware to the latest GA build before changing cables.
Force the refresh rate to 60 Hz in System Settings → Displays. Variable refresh on macOS 14.x has known compatibility issues with certain LG and Dell panels.
If the flicker only happens on battery, the dock is starved of power. Use the dock’s barrel-plug PSU — bus-powered docks cannot sustain dual 4K output.

articles.title: Returning a loaner laptop
body: Sign out of iCloud, Google Workspace, and the corporate VPN before returning the loaner. A factory reset runs automatically on first boot at the depot.
Pack the laptop with its original charger and any accessories you received. The depot rejects returns that arrive without a complete kit, even if the laptop itself is fine.
Drop off the loaner at the depot reception desk on Floor 3. You will receive a return confirmation email within one business day.

articles.title: Floor printer driver install
body: Run the `printer-bind` script from Self Service. The script discovers the nearest pull-print printer and installs the secure-release driver without admin rights.
All floor printers require badge release. After sending the job, tap your badge on any printer’s release pad within 4 hours or the job is purged.
If the script fails with error 0x80070005, the user account is missing the Print Spooler permission — open a ticket and assign it to the Desktop Engineering queue.

articles.title: Docking station firmware policy
body: Dock firmware updates ship quarterly through the IT Asset channel. Skipping an update is allowed but the dock will surface a banner on every connect reminding the user to schedule the update.
Only firmware signed by the dock vendor is allowed. The fleet ships with Secure Boot keys that refuse unsigned images, so do not attempt to flash third-party firmware.
After a firmware update the dock reboots once; this interrupts any active display stream. Plan updates around meetings, demos, or all-hands.

articles.title: Two-factor recovery codes
body: Each account receives ten single-use recovery codes at enrollment. Store them in the corporate password manager — paper copies in your desk drawer are not sufficient.
If you lose your phone, sign in with a recovery code and re-enroll a new device. Old codes remain valid; they do not get revoked when a new device is added.
To regenerate codes, open your account security settings and click “Regenerate”. The old codes stop working the moment the new codes are generated.

articles.title: Visitor Wi-Fi access
body: The visitor SSID is `corp-guest` and is open. Visitors are prompted for a voucher code on first connect; the code is single-use and expires after 12 hours.
Hosts generate voucher codes from the lobby kiosk. Each visitor must have a named sponsor who remains in the building for the duration of the visit.
If the visitor needs access to internal services, the sponsor must file a temporary access request at least two business days in advance.

articles.title: Corporate Wi-Fi profile setup
body: The corporate SSID is `corp-secure`. It uses WPA2-Enterprise with EAP-TLS. The client certificate is auto-provisioned on enrolment.
On macOS the profile is delivered through the MDM channel; on Windows it ships via Intune. Do not manually import the certificate — the MDM-managed identity is the only trusted one.
If the profile fails to install, check that the device clock is within 5 minutes of network time. A skewed clock is the most common cause of EAP-TLS handshake failures.

articles.title: DNS resolver policy
body: All corporate endpoints use the internal DoH resolver at `https://dns.corp.internal/dns-query`. The resolver enforces split-horizon DNS — internal names resolve to RFC1918 addresses.
If the DoH endpoint is unreachable, the client falls back to the OS default resolver. Fallback traffic is logged and may be denied for internal-only names.
Do not disable the resolver service to “fix” slow DNS. The slowdown is usually a network path issue, not a resolver issue; capture a trace and open a ticket.

articles.title: Endpoint backup retention
body: Every managed endpoint has a 90-day rolling backup. Files deleted from the device remain restorable for 90 days; after that the snapshot is purged.
The backup excludes the user’s Downloads folder and any directory tagged with the `nobackup` extended attribute. Mark scratch space with `nobackup` to keep it out of the snapshot.
A restore drill runs quarterly. The IT team picks five random endpoints and verifies the restore; you may be asked to keep the device plugged in overnight.

articles.title: OS upgrade window policy
body: OS upgrades are released GA+30. This delay lets the vendor’s first patch land before we deploy at scale, which materially reduces the rollback rate.
Critical updates (security advisories with CVSS ≥ 9) are exempted from the GA+30 delay and may deploy within 24 hours of release.
If an upgrade breaks a critical application on your device, file a rollback request within 7 days. Rollbacks after day 7 require a manual image and are reserved for fleet-wide issues.

articles.title: Phishing report workflow
body: Use the Report Phishing button in Outlook or the Slack `/report-phish` shortcut. Both routes land in the same triage queue within 60 seconds.
The triage team has a 30-minute SLA during business hours. After triage, malicious messages are purged from every mailbox in the tenant.
Never forward a suspicious message to a colleague to “ask if it’s real���. The triage team needs the original headers, which a forward strips.

articles.title: Full-disk encryption policy
body: Every managed device ships with full-disk encryption enabled (FileVault on macOS, BitLocker on Windows). Encryption is enforced by the MDM channel and cannot be disabled by the user.
The recovery key is escrowed to the corporate identity provider. A user who forgets their password can recover the key through the self-service portal without opening a ticket.
If the recovery portal is unavailable, the device must be re-imaged. This is intentional: the recovery key is the only path back into the encrypted volume.

articles.title: New hire onboarding pack
body: New hire packs ship to the manager 5 business days before the start date. The pack includes a laptop, dock, monitor, and accessories selected from the role’s hardware matrix.
Accounts are provisioned the morning of day one. The manager receives a welcome email with the new hire’s temporary password and a list of the SaaS apps they have been granted.
On day one, the new hire meets their onboarding buddy for a 30-minute orientation. The buddy walks them through the device, the password manager, and the request portal.

articles.title: Offboarding checklist
body: The offboarding workflow runs the day after the employee’s last day. Accounts are disabled, devices are requested for return, and the manager is asked to nominate a data custodian.
Email is forwarded to the manager for 30 days. After 30 days the mailbox is archived; the archive is searchable for 7 years per the corporate retention policy.

Files in the employee’s personal drive (OneDrive) are transferred to the data custodian. Personal files in the device’s local folders are not retained; the user is responsible for moving them before they leave.

articles.title: Internal transfer workflow
body: Internal transfers retain the existing device unless the new role’s hardware matrix requires a swap. The matrix is enforced by the HR feed; if the matrix says the new role needs a MacBook Pro 16″, the swap is automatic.
Access changes run through the IGA platform. The new role’s group memberships are added and the old role’s memberships are revoked. There is no manual override for this step.
The transfer is visible in the request portal as a single ticket. The ticket closes when the access review and the hardware swap (if any) are both complete.

articles.title: Headset pairing & audio quality
body: Bluetooth headsets paired to multiple devices can stutter when two devices stream audio at the same time. Disable Bluetooth on the second device during calls for the best quality.
USB headsets take priority over Bluetooth in the OS audio routing. If a USB headset is plugged in but the system is playing through Bluetooth, quit and reopen the audio app to force a re-routing.
Firmware updates for the corporate headsets ship through the device management channel. The update is silent and takes about 90 seconds.

articles.title: VPN failover to backup gateway
body: The primary VPN gateway runs a health check every 30 seconds. If two consecutive checks fail, the client automatically falls over to the backup gateway.

Manual failover is available from the VPN client’s menu. Use it when the primary gateway is sluggish but not yet flagged as failed; the client will return to the primary once the health check recovers.
If both gateways are unavailable, the client logs an error and the user should connect via the mobile hotspot until the gateways recover.

articles.title: Incident severity and SLA
body: Incidents are classified P1 through P3. P1 is a complete outage affecting more than 50 users; P2 is a degraded service affecting a team; P3 is a single-user issue.
P1 targets: 15-minute response, 4-hour resolution. P2 targets: 1-hour response, 1-business-day resolution. P3 targets: 1-business-day response, 5-business-day resolution.
Severity can be reclassified during an incident. The on-call lead has the authority to upgrade or downgrade, and any change is logged on the incident timeline.

articles.title: Zero-trust access for SaaS
body: All SaaS access is gated by conditional access. The policy requires a managed device, an MFA challenge, and a compliant posture (encryption on, OS up to date).

Unmanaged devices can read public documents but cannot access internal-only SaaS. The policy enforces this at the identity provider, not at the SaaS app, so the user sees a single, consistent experience.
If a user is travelling and the managed device fails the posture check, they can request a temporary exception from the on-call lead. Exceptions are time-boxed to 24 hours.

articles.title: Internal load balancer health checks
body: Internal load balancers probe `/healthz` on every backend. The probe must return 200 within 200 ms; otherwise the backend is taken out of rotation.
When a backend is being drained for maintenance, the load balancer stops sending new requests but allows in-flight requests to complete. Draining is non-disruptive and reversible.
If a backend is consistently failing the probe, check the application logs first. The most common cause is a missing database connection, not a load-balancer misconfiguration.
